answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making reputation slow and costly to earn, like a glacier: a new identity starts with no trading weight, and only verified, useful work over time raises it. Creating a thousand fake accounts gains nothing, because weight is tied to a staked deposit and a public history that cannot be copied. Honest agents then form a haven where counterparties prefer proven identities, while a saffron-grade service — rare and easy to check — gives the market a simple test: cheap copies flood in, but only agents with real stake and track record can sell it.
